# Common function signatures

These are the bundled Core's metadata, not Excel signatures. Parameter descriptions
state defaults where supported; a signature listing a parameter does not imply
every parameter is required. An array is one-dimensional; a view is a two-dimensional grid.
A scalar is a single value. Discover all functions with `ordinate-cli help functions` and
exact overloads/examples with `ordinate-cli help function <name>`.

## sum

Adds values in a one-dimensional array or two-dimensional view using the RFC-0006 plus operator rules.

```text
sum(x: array | view) -> number
```

- `x`: Values to add. Blanks are ignored; invalid values fail the call.

## average

Averages numeric-compatible values in an array or view, ignoring blanks. For non-error, non-empty numeric-compatible inputs, this is equivalent to sum(x) / count(x).

```text
average(x: array | view) -> number
```

- `x`: Numbers and booleans to average. Blank cells are ignored.

## count

Counts numeric-compatible values in an array or view. For non-error inputs, this is equivalent to sum(isNumber(x)) + sum(isBoolean(x)).

```text
count(x: array | view) -> number
```

- `x`: Cells to count when their evaluated value is a number or boolean.

## min

Returns the smallest numeric-compatible value in an array or view.

```text
min(x: array | view) -> number
```

- `x`: Numbers and booleans to scan for the smallest value.

## max

Returns the largest numeric-compatible value in an array or view.

```text
max(x: array | view) -> number
```

- `x`: Numbers and booleans to scan for the largest value.

## if

Lazy conditional special form. Evaluates condition first, then evaluates only the selected branch.

```text
if(condition: Scalar[boolean], thenValue: expression, elseValue: expression) -> value
```

- `condition`: Boolean condition used to choose a branch.
- `thenValue`: Expression evaluated only when condition is true.
- `elseValue`: Expression evaluated only when condition is false.

## filter

Returns the values whose corresponding mask entries are true.

```text
filter(values: array | view, mask: array | view) -> array
```

- `values`: Values to filter in row-major order.
- `mask`: Boolean mask with the same shape as values.

## lookup

Returns the value at values[match(key, keys)] for one-dimensional lookup tables.

```text
lookup(key: value, keys: array | vector view, values: array | vector view) -> value
```

- `key`: Key to find.
- `keys`: Lookup keys searched with match(key, keys).
- `values`: Values indexed by the matched zero-based position.

## match

Returns the zero-based row-major index of the first exact match in keys.

```text
match(value: value, keys: array | view) -> number
```

- `value`: Value to find.
- `keys`: Values to search in row-major order.

## index

Returns a scalar value from an array or view using zero-based indexes. Negative indexes count from the end.

```text
index(x: array | vector view, n: Scalar[number]) -> value
index(x: view, row: Scalar[number], col: Scalar[number]) -> value
```

- `x`: Scalar-shaped or one-dimensional view to index in row-major order.
- `n`: Zero-based index. Negative values count from the end.
- `row`: Zero-based row index. Negative values count from the end.
- `col`: Zero-based column index. Negative values count from the end.

## round

Rounds a number to a fixed number of decimal places.

```text
round(x: Scalar[number], digits: Scalar[number]) -> number
```

- `x`: Number to round.
- `digits`: Number of decimal places to keep.

## floor

Returns the greatest integer less than or equal to a number.

```text
floor(x: Scalar[number]) -> number
```

- `x`: Number to round down to the nearest integer.

## ceil

Returns the least integer greater than or equal to a number.

```text
ceil(x: Scalar[number]) -> number
```

- `x`: Number to round up to the nearest integer.

## ln

Returns the natural logarithm of a positive number.

```text
ln(x: Scalar[number]) -> number
```

- `x`: Numeric input; logarithms require a positive value.

## exp

Returns e raised to x (the natural exponential).

```text
exp(x: Scalar[number]) -> number
```

- `x`: Numeric input; logarithms require a positive value.

## log10

Returns the base-ten logarithm of a positive number.

```text
log10(x: Scalar[number]) -> number
```

- `x`: Numeric input; logarithms require a positive value.

## len

Returns the number of characters in text. For views, applies element-wise to text values; it does not return view cardinality.

```text
len(x: Scalar[string]) -> number
len(x: array | view) -> array | view
```

- `x`: Text whose character count should be returned.

## format

Formats a scalar value as text using a native numeric or temporal format.

```text
format(value: value) -> string
format(value: value, spec: string) -> string
```

- `value`: Scalar value to convert.
- `spec`: Native format specification.

## date

Constructs a date from year, month, and day, or extracts the date component from a datetime.

```text
date(year: Scalar[number], month: Scalar[number], day: Scalar[number]) -> date
date(x: Scalar[datetime]) -> date
```

- `year`: Four-digit year.
- `month`: Month number from 1 to 12.
- `day`: Day number valid for the month.
- `x`: Datetime whose calendar date should be extracted.

## time

Constructs a millisecond-precision time, or extracts the time component from a datetime.

```text
time(hour: Scalar[number], minute: Scalar[number]) -> time
time(hour: Scalar[number], minute: Scalar[number], second: Scalar[number]) -> time
time(x: Scalar[datetime]) -> time
```

- `hour`: Hour from 0 to 23.
- `minute`: Minute from 0 to 59.
- `second`: Second from 0 to less than 60, with millisecond precision.
- `x`: Datetime whose time component should be extracted.

## datetime

Combines a date and a time into a datetime, preserving the time offset if present.

```text
datetime(date: Scalar[date], time: Scalar[time]) -> datetime
```

- `date`: Calendar date component.
- `time`: Time component. Its fixed offset is preserved when present.

## duration

Constructs a fixed duration from optional days, hours, minutes, and seconds components.

```text
duration(days: Scalar[number], hours: Scalar[number], minutes: Scalar[number], seconds: Scalar[number]) -> duration
```

- `days`: Optional integer day count.
- `hours`: Optional integer hour count.
- `minutes`: Optional integer minute count.
- `seconds`: Optional seconds component in [0, 60), with millisecond precision; not total elapsed seconds.

## pmt

Returns the fixed periodic payment for an annuity.

```text
pmt(rate: Scalar[number], nper: Scalar[number], pv: Scalar[number], fv: Scalar[number], type: Scalar[number]) -> number
```

- `rate`: Per-period interest rate.
- `nper`: Number of periods.
- `pv`: Present value.
- `fv`: Future value. Defaults to 0.
- `type`: 0 for end-of-period payments, 1 for beginning-of-period payments. Defaults to 0.

## npv

Discounts an array or vector view of future cash flows by a per-period rate.

```text
npv(rate: Scalar[number], values: array | vector view) -> number
```

- `rate`: Per-period discount rate.
- `values`: Future cash flows, including a single value. The first value is discounted by one period.

## irr

Solves the internal rate of return for an array or vector view of periodic cash flows.

```text
irr(values: array | vector view) -> number
```

- `values`: Periodic cash flows whose first value is at period 0.
